hook: A short file about a silent heap of gears that has to be kept rusting in seawater. Read it as a mood piece; much of the unease comes from the precise, oddly specific procedures. The tags link it to the Broken God, but you need no background to enjoy it.
whyItMatters: It is a compact way into the clockwork imagery tied to the Broken God, a theme that recurs across the site. A machine that grows by swallowing metal, and draws people toward it with noises only they can hear, is a strong and simple hook. It also shows how a featured article can work with just a few paragraphs and some well-chosen loose threads.
thingsToNotice:
The central contradiction is the best touch: the object makes no sound at all, yet those who linger near it hear grinding and clicking that only eases when they feed it.

The recovery notes do a lot with little, a circle scrubbed clean of metal and a small town left empty nearby, and let you fill in the rest. Rust itself is the containment, so decay is the one thing keeping the machine still. The cross-references at the end point to a wider web without stopping to explain it.

related.note: The containment note warns to keep anyone touched by it away from this machine.
Played on loop during recovery to calm the mechanism enough to approach.
